blocks.text: By Email
Re: Engagement for Prosecution Support, Keith-Duarte Pending Applications
Dear Mr. Palmer:

Thank you for asking Hollowell Patent Group PLLC to support {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} in the prosecution of its pending United States patent applications. This letter sets out what we will do, who will do it, what it will cost, and the terms on which we will act. If any part of it does not match what you understood the company to be asking for, please raise it with me before you sign.
The Engagement

The company has asked us to take responsibility for prosecuting the pending United States applications that it identifies to us in writing at or before the start of the engagement, which this letter calls the designated applications. For each designated application we will review the file history, docket every response date and fee window against the records of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, prepare and file responses to office actions, conduct examiner interviews where we judge one likely to help, and handle allowance and issue fee matters on your instruction.

Before any designated application issues, we will give you a written recommendation on whether a continuation should be filed to preserve claim scope that the allowed claims may not reach, so that the company can make that decision while the option still exists. The filing of a continuation or of any other new application would be a separate matter, estimated and agreed in writing before we begin it.
Matters Outside the Engagement

Unless we agree otherwise in writing, the engagement does not include the drafting of new applications, prosecution before patent offices outside the United States, post-grant or inter partes proceedings, litigation, or any opinion on the validity, enforceability, or infringement of any patent. If such a question arises, we will tell you and will not take it up until its scope and cost are agreed.
How We Will Proceed

We will proceed in three steps, of which the first must be complete before the other two properly begin. First, we will obtain each file history, confirm every pending date against the official record, and enter those dates on our docket. Second, for each open office action we will send you a short summary of the rejections, the response date, and the course we recommend; third, we will prepare each response, send you the draft well before its due date, and file it on your instruction.

If any designated application is now in the care of other counsel, we will file a new power of attorney and request the file, and until the transfer is recorded we will treat its dates as ours to meet.
The Team

Heather Munoz, a Partner in our prosecution group, will lead the engagement, will review every response before it is filed, and will sign any response that changes the scope of a claim. Kelly Snyder, an Associate, will be your day-to-day contact, will prepare most of the responses, and will keep you informed of the docket as dates approach.

Joseph Walker, an Associate, will analyze the references cited in prior art rejections and will prepare the technical side of any examiner interview. I will remain responsible for the firm's relationship with the company and for the terms of this letter, and you should call me directly if anything about the engagement is not working as it should.
We will take instructions from you, as General Manager, or from any person you name to us in writing. We will not act on an instruction that comes from anyone else.
Conflict Check

Before sending this letter we searched our records for any current or former representation adverse to {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}, and the search disclosed none. If you know of a competitor, licensee, or other party whose interests could be adverse to the company in this work, please tell us before you sign, so that we can run the search again with that party included.
Fee and Start of Work

Our fee for the work described in this letter is a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2021-001.fee}}. Work will begin on {{fact:f:E-2021-001.start}}, provided that by that date we have received a signed copy of this letter and the company's written list of designated applications.

The fixed fee covers our professional services only. Official fees of the Patent and Trademark Office and similar out-of-pocket costs will be billed separately at our cost, and we will not pay an official fee without your prior approval unless it is needed to prevent a loss of rights at a time when we cannot reach you.
Invoices and Payment

We will invoice the fixed fee in equal monthly installments over the expected term of the engagement, together with any official fees and costs advanced during the month, and each invoice is due on receipt. If an invoice remains unpaid when the following month's invoice is issued, we may suspend work, and if the balance then remains unpaid after written notice, we may withdraw, in each case only to the extent the rules of professional conduct permit.

Suspension or withdrawal for nonpayment will not leave a date unattended. Before we stop work for any reason, we will write to you listing every response date and fee deadline then pending in the designated applications, and we will protect those dates until responsibility for them has passed to the company or to other counsel.
Duration and Termination

The engagement runs from the start date until we have completed the work described in this letter, unless it ends earlier. The company may end it at any time by written notice, and we may do so where the rules of professional conduct permit or require, including for nonpayment.

When the engagement ends, for whatever reason, we will send you a closing letter listing every date then pending in the designated applications, and from the date of that letter the company will be responsible for those dates unless we have agreed in writing to continue. Installments invoiced before the end, and official fees already advanced, remain payable.
Confidential Information

We will hold in confidence the invention disclosures, technical documents, and business information that the company gives us, and we will not disclose them outside the company without your consent. Our communications with you about the designated applications will be treated as privileged to the extent the law allows.

There is one limit on that undertaking. The company's inventors and this firm each owe the Patent and Trademark Office a duty to disclose information known to be material to patentability, and if we learn of a reference that must be disclosed, we will tell you and file it.
Limits on Our Responsibility

The outcome of prosecution depends on examiners and on the prior art, neither of which we control, and we cannot promise that any application will be allowed, or that it will issue with claims of any particular scope or within any particular time. Our recommendations will be professional judgments on the record available to us, and they will be qualified accordingly.

Where the rules of professional conduct allow a limit, the firm's total liability arising out of this engagement will not exceed the fees the company has paid under this letter. Where those rules do not allow a limit, this paragraph does not apply.
Applicable Law
This letter, and any dispute arising out of it or out of the engagement, is governed by the law of the state in which our office is located, without regard to that state's rules on conflicts of law.
Acceptance

If these terms are acceptable, please sign below and return a signed copy to me by email. Once it arrives, Kelly Snyder will send you a short list of the documents we need for intake, beginning with the company's own docket records for the designated applications.
Sincerely yours,
Kickoff Memorandum

To: Kelly Snyder; Joseph Walker
From: Heather Munoz
Re: Keith-Duarte prosecution support
What we owe the client

Every pending application on the {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} list moves forward, and no date is missed. That is the whole job. The engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2021-001.start}}, and the fee is fixed.
Our contact is Joseph Palmer, General Manager. He wants the recommendation first and the reasons after it. Instructions come from him, or from someone he names in writing, and from no one else.
We are not drafting new applications on this matter, and we are not giving validity or infringement opinions. If Keith-Duarte asks for either, bring it to me before anyone says yes.
The work, in the order it starts

items: Intake and docket. Kelly Snyder pulls the file history for every designated application and checks each response date and fee window against the Patent Office record. Docketing enters the dates and a second person checks them. If a date falls inside the intake period, tell me the same day.

Office action summaries. Kelly Snyder writes one page per open action: the rejections, the response date, the path we recommend, and a rough cost. If the path looks expensive for this client, say so on the page.

Prior art rejections. Joseph Walker reads the cited references against the claims. For each rejection, mark whether argument alone is likely to be enough or whether we need an amendment. Nothing goes out with a conclusion I have not seen qualified.
Inventor call. I will ask Joseph Palmer for a technical call with the inventors on the application with the earliest response date.
Continuation watch. I keep a running list of applications that look close to allowance. No issue fee is paid until the client has our continuation recommendation in writing.

blocks.text: Budget
The fee is fixed, so time spent outside the letter is ours to absorb. Track your hours against each application anyway. If one application starts to take more than its share, I want to know early.
Continuations sit outside the fee. When we recommend one, the client gets a cost estimate in the same letter.
Writing to Keith-Duarte
Anything that goes to the client leads with the decision needed and the date it is needed by. The analysis comes second. Caveats go in their own paragraph, where they cannot be skimmed past.
Use full names and titles in anything Joseph Palmer reads. Every draft response comes to me before it goes to him. I sign any response that changes claim scope.
What could go wrong early

items: Files held by other counsel. If any application has not transferred yet, its dates are still ours to watch. Kelly Snyder should flag each one until the power of attorney is recorded.
Client records that disagree with the official record. The Patent Office record controls. Note every mismatch, and tell the client which dates we corrected.
Inventor availability. If the inventors cannot meet before the first response is due, we file on the record we have and say so in the response summary.

blocks.text: Before we meet again

items: Kelly Snyder: request the file histories and the client's own docket records. Send me the reconciled date list when it is done.
Joseph Walker: open a prior art file for each application, starting with the earliest response date.
Heather Munoz: confirm the designated application list with Joseph Palmer in writing, and ask for the inventor call.

blocks.text: Date questions come to me the day you find them. Everything else can wait for our weekly meeting.
Dear Joseph,

The {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} docket is reconciled, and none of the pending response dates or fee windows is at risk. A few dates in the company's own tracking did not match the Patent Office record; we have docketed the official dates and will send you the corrected list this week.

Each open office action now has a one-page summary, and the response with the earliest due date is in draft. We have started reading the references cited against your claims in that application. Nothing we have seen so far changes the approach set out in our engagement letter.

We need a call of about an hour with the inventors on that application, within the next two weeks if possible, so that we can test our reading of the references before the draft comes to you for review. Separately, please tell us in writing whether the company wants a continuation recommendation on every application before allowance, or only on the ones you name.
If you suggest two or three times that suit the inventors, my colleagues copied here will send a short agenda ahead of the call.

Best,
Heather
Keith-Duarte Prosecution Support: Notes of Working Session

We ended the session in agreement that the first two responses can be finalized on the approach we have been taking, and that the application drawing closest to allowance needs a written decision from {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} on a continuation before it goes any further.
Attendees

items: Joseph Palmer, General Manager, Keith-Duarte
Heather Munoz, Partner
Kelly Snyder, Associate
Joseph Walker, Associate (notes)

blocks.text: Discussion

Heather Munoz opened by noting that the docket remains clean, and Kelly Snyder confirmed that every response date we hold has now been checked twice against the Patent Office record, so we were able to spend the session on substance rather than on dates, which is where we hoped these meetings would be by this stage of the engagement.

Joe took us through the references cited against the earliest application, and our shared reading is that the main rejection can be answered by argument, although one dependent claim will likely need a narrowing amendment to stay clear of the second reference. Heather Munoz asked that the draft say plainly that this is our judgment of how the examiner will read the art and not a certainty, and Joseph Palmer said he was comfortable with that framing going to the file.

On the second application, where the examiner has combined two references against the independent claim, Joe's view is that the combination is weaker than the action makes it sound, and Heather Munoz suggested we keep an examiner interview in reserve, since a well-argued written response may do the work on its own and an interview can still follow if it does not.

Joseph Palmer told us that the inventors came away from last month's call satisfied with how we had described the device, and we agreed that any further technical questions will go to him first, so that we use the inventors' time only where it changes what we file.

Kelly Snyder raised the cost side of the continuation question directly, reminding us that a continuation sits outside the fixed fee and that filing on more than one application in a short span would be a real expense for the company. Joseph Palmer took the point and asked us to recommend a continuation only where the allowed claims would plainly leave a product feature uncovered, which is the standard we will hold ourselves to.

We closed with a word on format. Joseph Palmer asked that future summaries lead with the decision he needs to make and the date by which he needs to make it, and we were glad to hear it, because that is how Kelly Snyder has been writing them already.
Action Items

rows: Finalize the response on the earliest application, keeping the qualified language on the dependent claim
Joe, with review by Heather Munoz
Send the written continuation recommendation on the application nearest allowance, with a cost estimate
Confirm in writing whether the company wants a continuation on that application
Recast the remaining office action summaries in the new format, decision and date first

blocks.text: The next step is Heather Munoz's written continuation recommendation, which goes to Joseph Palmer by the end of next week so that his answer can come back to us before the application moves again.
Prosecution Support: Status at the Midpoint
Prepared for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} by Heather Munoz, Partner, with Kelly Snyder and Joseph Walker, Associates.
Where Things Stand
The engagement is on schedule at about its halfway point. No response date has been missed, and none is at risk. Work to date sits inside the fixed fee.
The first response has been filed and the second is in final draft. The main open item is the company's decision on a continuation for the application that appears closest to allowance.
Completed So Far

items: Docket reconciliation. Every pending response date and fee window in the designated applications has been checked against the Patent Office record and entered on our docket. Kelly Snyder rechecks the list each month.
Office action summaries. Each open action has a one-page summary showing the rejections, the response date, and our recommended path. The summaries now lead with the decision needed and its date.
Inventor call. The call with the inventors on the earliest application took place as planned. It confirmed our reading of the device.
First response. The response on the earliest application was filed after the company approved the draft. It answers the main rejection by argument and narrows one dependent claim.
Prior art review. Joseph Walker has finished his review of the references cited in the second application. His notes are with me and are reflected in the final draft.
Continuation recommendation. Our written recommendation on the application closest to allowance has gone to the company, with a cost estimate.

rows: Review the next action when it issues

blocks.text: Next in Line
The remaining work in scope, in the order we expect to take it up:

items: File the second response once the company approves the final draft.
Act on the company's continuation decision as soon as it arrives.
Answer any new office action in the same summary format, with the draft sent for review well before its due date.
Request an examiner interview on the second application if the written response alone does not look likely to move the examiner.

blocks.text: Each item will reach the company with the decision and its date stated first, as the summaries do now. Drafts will arrive well before their due dates.
Budget
The fixed fee for the engagement is {{fact:f:E-2021-001.fee}}. Work to date falls within it. We expect the remaining work in scope to fall within it as well.

Two kinds of cost sit outside the fee. Official Patent Office fees are billed at cost, as the engagement letter provides. A continuation filing would be a separate matter, estimated in writing before we start.
Kelly Snyder prepared the cost estimate that accompanies our continuation recommendation. It is there so the company can weigh the expense against the claim scope at stake.
Risks
None of the following is serious today. Each could become serious if it is left alone.

items: Continuation timing. If the application is allowed before the company decides, the time to act shortens. Once the patent issues, a continuation can no longer be filed from it.
Examiner response. The argument on the main claim in the first response is, in our judgment, the stronger position. The examiner may not accept it, and a further amendment may then be needed.
Docket changes. A new office action or a notice of allowance sets new dates on that application. Kelly Snyder enters each new date the day the notice arrives and confirms it to the company.

Late office actions. An action that issues late in the engagement may carry a response date that falls after the engagement ends. We will list any such date for the company in writing before we close.

blocks.text: Decisions Needed From the Company
Two decisions are open. The first is urgent and the second is not.

items: Continuation. Please confirm in writing whether the company wants a continuation filed on the application closest to allowance. Our recommendation and the cost estimate set out the basis for each choice.
Second response. Please approve the final draft, or send comments, so that it can be filed well ahead of its due date.

blocks.text: Questions
Please send questions on any item to me or to Kelly Snyder. The decision we need first from Keith-Duarte is the continuation instruction.
Closing Working Session: Prosecution Support for Keith-Duarte

We finished the working part of the engagement today with every designated application in a settled position and every pending date accounted for, so what remains is the closing letter that hands the docket back to {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}.
Present

items: Joseph Palmer, General Manager, Keith-Duarte
Heather Munoz, Partner
Kelly Snyder, Associate
Joseph Walker, Associate, who kept these notes

blocks.text: What We Covered

Heather Munoz began with the application that had been closest to allowance, where the company decided, after reading our recommendation and the cost estimate with it, not to pursue a continuation, and the issue fee was paid on its written instruction. Joseph Palmer said again that the allowed claims reach the features the company sells today, and Heather Munoz noted for the file that the decision was his to make and was made with the cost and the risk both in front of him.

Kelly Snyder then took us through the remaining applications one at a time, and we agreed that the second response moved the examiner on the main claim, that the rejection still standing there is a narrow one, and that the next action on it is not expected until after the engagement ends, which means its date belongs on the closing list rather than on our own calendar.

Joseph Walker summarized where the prior art work leaves things: the references the examiners have relied on so far have each been answered, and nothing new has come to our attention that would need to be disclosed, though he was careful to say that this reflects what we have seen in the course of prosecution and is not the result of a search of the field.

We spent the rest of our time on the handover, because that is the point in an engagement where a date can fall between two desks. Joseph Palmer asked that the closing letter go to him with a copy to whoever at the company will hold the docket, and he will name that person in writing; Heather Munoz added that we would be glad to take the applications back up if the company asks.

Kelly Snyder confirmed that the work in scope was completed within the fixed fee, and that the only further charges will be the official fees already paid on the company's instruction, which will appear on the final invoice with their receipts. Joseph Palmer asked that we keep a complete copy of the file after the documents go back, and we confirmed that we will hold it under our usual retention practice.

Prepare the closing letter listing every pending response date and fee window in the designated applications
Once the docket holder is named
Review and sign the closing letter
Return the company's original documents and confirm the file index
